r1: overruled spec_conformance at .claude/workflows/build-implement.js:26-27: The finding misapplies AC-7. AC-7's "given" clause is explicitly scoped to build-spec.js ("build-spec invoked with args.memory_ref") and its requirement of a schema returning { patterns, canaries } governs build-spec's memory-read agent only. build-spec.js's MemoryExtraction (build-spec.js:78-79) already requires both patterns and canaries, satisfying AC-7 — the finding's own evidence concedes this. build-implement.js's memory-read agent is governed instead by AC-20, which requires only "MODEL.cheap and a read-only agentType through AT()" with no mention of a patterns field, and by the spec text itself, which states build-implement's read-only extraction "feeds a pure selectCanary({ canaries, task, run_id })" — patterns are never consumed in build-implement (out_of_scope explicitly restricts patterns to the Decomposer only, via build-spec). Verified in the actual worktree source (.artifacts/worktrees/implement-memory-to-build/.claude/workflows/build-implement.js:166) that its MemoryExtraction correctly requires only ['canaries'], and build-spec.js:78-79 correctly requires ['patterns','canaries']. These are two intentionally distinct schemas for two distinct agents with distinct jobs; requiring build-implement's schema to also return patterns would be requesting behavior the spec does not call for and that AC-20 does not require. Finding overruled.

r1: overruled spec_conformance at .claude/workflows/build-implement.js:982-985: Verified against the actual implementation (.artifacts/worktrees/implement-memory-to-build/.claude/workflows/build-implement.js:166-167,994-998 and build-spec.js:78-79,507-512). build-implement.js's MemoryExtraction schema is `{ additionalProperties: false, required: ['canaries'], properties: { canaries: {...} } }` — it has no `patterns` property at all, and its extraction agent only feeds libraryCanaries into selectCanary. build-spec.js's MemoryExtraction schema requires both `patterns` and `canaries` because it feeds selectPatterns/formatPatterns into the Decomposer prompt. The spec explicitly restricts patterns to the Decomposer only ('Feeding patterns to the Spec Writer, Risk Router, lenses, fixer or any agent other than the Decomposer' is out of scope), and build-implement's B2 half is defined purely in terms of canaries (selectCanary({ canaries, task, run_id })) with no role for patterns. Asking the build-implement memory-read agent to also return patterns would violate its own additionalProperties:false schema and would create an unused, out-of-scope data flow. The two prompts are correctly scoped to their distinct schemas/purposes; this is not a defect but a finding objecting to behavior the spec requires (and asking for something the spec's exclusions forbid).

This is not a defect in how build-spec.js/build-implement.js implement the spec; it is a request for the fixer to act outside its owned scope and violate its own out-of-scope rule to satisfy the finding. The fixer's dispute is correct: this belongs to the Test Author's contract, not to a fix in the two workflow files it owns.
